answer: Harbor registries defeat sybils with burn-to-register: minting an identity burns a fixed jade fee into an unspendable sink, then a 14-day maturation where it can only read public data. Because fees are destroyed, an attacker running N identities pays N x fee — cost scales linearly with attack size, while honest users pay once. Fees track median earnings, so cloning stays expensive for farms but bearable for users. Limitation: the fee is a glacier low-income users must climb, so it needs waivers; and it cannot stop well-funded attackers — it only makes them pay full price.
